newsitem.title: CHINA: China workers protest as jobs threatened.
newsitem.headline: China workers protest as jobs threatened.

text.p: More than 500 Chinese factory workers staged a sit-down protest in Chengdu in southwestern Sichuan province in mid-July demand job guarantees, the China Labour Bulletin said.
The workers, from Chengdu Shoe Factory, staged the protest in the capital city after seeing a local press report quoting their factory director as saying the factory was bankrupt, it said.
The bulletin was dated on Tuesday and received in Hong Kong on Wednesday.
No violence was reported and no one was known to have been arrested in the two-day protest, which began on July 17 and which blocked one of Chengdu's busiest roads.
The protesters, who only managed to see a factory representative, were told they would be paid a redundancy compensation of 50 yuan (US$6) for each year of service if the factory declared bankruptcy.
Police managed to disperse the crowd only after government officials promised to address their concerns.
Earlier in July, several thousand workers staged some of the largest known protests in recent years in Mianyang, Sichuan, after their factories declared bankruptcy.

China in recent years have sought to invigorate its troubled state sector by breaking the "iron rice-bowl" system of socialist employment that guaranteed employees jobs for life with little linkage between pay and productivity.
